text:
mika (People Ops): Hi @tess — Owen just converted from contractor to W-2 mid-pay-period and says his direct deposit was much lower than expected. He shared a stub showing both a contractor payout and W-2 earnings with federal tax that looks like FICA + a large federal withholding. Can payroll confirm how the mid-month conversion was taxed?

tess (Payroll): Can you paste the redacted stub or last4 so I can pull the runs? Also what were the effective dates of conversion?

mika (People Ops): Redacted snippet Owen DM'd: 
```
Pay period 09/01/2026 - 09/15/2026
Contractor payout (1099): $2,400.00
W-2 earnings (conversion prorate): $1,800.00
Federal tax withheld: $1,140.00
FICA (OASDI+Med): $138.00
Net deposit: $2,922.00
```
Employee: Owen Blake, EmpID 53012, last4 3344. Conversion effective 09/07/2026; contractor invoice was paid 09/10 before HR flagged the conversion.

owen (Eng): I thought contractor runs stop once conversion effective date is set. I submitted conversion paperwork on 09/05 and signed the W-2 offer on 09/06. Shouldn't the invoice after 09/07 have been blocked?

tess (Payroll): @payroll-bot fetch payroll + AP payout logs for EmpID 53012 for period 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-15.

payroll-bot: Pulling records... Found contractor AP payment (Invoice 9876) processed 2026-09-10 03:24Z and payroll W-2 earnings run on 2026-09-11 02:10Z. HRIS conversion flag set 2026-09-06 18:05Z but AP queue had a pending payment created 08/29 and auto-approved on business rules. System treated the invoice as a separate 1099 payment and applied no withholdings on that line; however the payroll engine later treated the W-2 prorated earnings and computed regular withholding PLUS applied supplemental federal withholding to the combined taxable amount because a single-day payroll import had mixed earning types. Creating ticket PAY-8345 to split flows, reverse incorrect supplemental portion and coordinate with AP for invoice hold policy.

mika (People Ops): So the main issue is AP timing + payroll importing mixed earnings in one run? Is the supplemental withholding the cause of the large federal figure?

tess (Payroll): Yes. The combined taxable gross triggered supplemental-path for the W-2 import in our current flow. AP paid the invoice which created a 1099-type payment; when payroll later processed conversion prorate in the same ledger cycle it didn't correctly isolate withholding flows. We'll manual-adjust: 1) reverse the supplemental withholding applied to W-2 prorate, 2) ensure contractor payout remains treated as non-withheld 1099 (reporting only), and 3) notify tax ops about 1099 vs W-2 split. Off-cycle adjustment will update YTD and (if needed) feed to year-end reporting. Ticket PAY-8345 will include mapping for 1099 box and W-2 box differences.

owen (Eng): Will I get a separate off-cycle refund or will it be a positive adjustment on next payroll? I have rent due Friday.

tess (Payroll): For payroll processing errors we can issue an off-cycle refund. ETA 2 business days to triage and 3 business days to execute payout. If AP can stop the invoice payment we can avoid the 1099 issuance but that ship appears sailed for this run; we'll coordinate with AP to see if reversal is possible. We'll cc you on PAY-8345 and can prioritize the refund as urgent.

hris-bot: HRIS log: Conversion effective flag set 2026-09-06 18:05Z; AP invoice 9876 auto-approved 2026-08-29 09:11Z; no AP hold requested.

mika (People Ops): I'll follow up with AP to request a reversal if possible and send Owen the ticket link. @tess please cc me on updates. Owen, sorry about the cashflow hit — we'll push to prioritize. :pray:

tess (Payroll): Will do. One more note: this flow can affect contractor/year-end reporting (1099) and W-2 aggregation. PAY-8345 will record whether a 1099 or a W-2 correction (W-2c/1099 correction) is needed depending on timing.

owen (Eng): Thanks all. Appreciate the speedy help.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from tess, :eyes: from mika)
